title: Baseline before any archive file
blurb: No records yet. This line starts from one sentence: Maria Demko was the wife of Mihaly Duska and the mother of Stefan, Kevin's paternal grandfather. Nothing is known of her birth year, village, parents or church. What Kevin said before the rebuild began is logged as priors, not findings: her birth record is thought to be in Uzhhorod, the family villages are Senné and Iňačovce, and he leans toward a Rusyn origin. A first pass through public catalogues shows the Greek Catholic books for Iňačovce held at Prešov stop in 1898, which may be why a later baptism would have to be sought in Uzhhorod. Eight hypotheses are on the board, each with a confidence and a named test.

title: Cicarovce: one baptism, 1882
blurb: One image, given with no context: a single line cut from a Hungarian-language baptism register. On 20 August 1882 a boy named Mihály was baptised, born the day before at Viszoka no. 132 to György Demkó, a Greek Catholic farmer, and Mária Hreskó, a Roman Catholic. This is the first Demko household on paper, and it sits in a village the priors never mentioned. Nothing in the entry ties it to Maria Demko. Mihály could be her brother, her father, or no relation, and the board now carries the first two as competing hypotheses with most of the weight still on 'unproven'. The mixed marriage matters either way: under the custom of the time a daughter of this couple would have been baptised Roman Catholic, which cuts against looking for Maria in a Greek Catholic book. No hypothesis is resolved. Five moved, three were raised.

title: Ledger v2 and notes from the other agents
blurb: No new file. Read ledger v2, the common rules, and the notes from the Duska and Site agents; read the Duska repo at 53bf7f0. Three things changed on the board. First, the coordinator withdrew the 1868 mixed-marriage rule as a constraint, and the Duska agent holds a counter-example (DUS:S-004), so half of the cut made in DM-B-001 to a Greek Catholic baptism for Maria is restored. Second, the collector's file names are priors and nothing more (X-004), which takes five points off the reading that Maria is a daughter of the Viszoka household. Third, the question 'not of that household at all' is now carried here as DM-H-012 at 50, so the three rival answers sum to 100. The Duska agent also reports a second György Demko, at Gönyű in 1895 with a different wife; this agent has not been given those images and rates 'same man' at 5. The Duska agent's independent reading of the 1882 strip agrees with DM-D-001 on every field. Work now lives on main, with a stamping workflow, a role file and a decisions list. Kevin has allowed open research on the Demko surname, excluding anything he wrote.

title: Research pass 1: the Demko surname
blurb: No new file. Kevin allowed open research on the Demko surname, excluding anything he wrote, and one pass was run. Its useful result concerns the 1882 strip. A village history lists Ján Csurgovics as Greek Catholic priest of Čičarovce from 1882 to 1886, and the Greek Catholics of Viszoka were served from Čičarovce, so the collector's label is probably right about the parish and the book is probably the Greek Catholic one. A second look at the strip itself complicates that: the entry beneath is signed by Polányi Endre, whom the same history names as the village's Roman Catholic priest. The page was written by clergy of both rites, which fits a village with three churches but does not say whose book it is. The pass found no Demko in a transcription of the 1715 tax lists for the four villages and nothing in North American indexes. It also reached into the owner's private correspondence and repeated two statements from it; those are set aside and reported to the coordinator. One hypothesis moved; none was raised or resolved.

title: Demko Documents: ten files, 1803 to 1966
blurb: The folder that puts Maria Demko on paper. A parish certificate issued at Senné in 1947 names the parents of Štefan Duska, born there on 21 October 1929, as Michal Duska of Senné and Maria Demko, Greek Catholic, of Iňačovce. A gravestone in Montréal reads Mary Demko, born 1906, died 1950, wife of Mike Duska, and a 1966 deed gives her death as 9 September 1950. A state birth registration of 1906 records a Mária born at Solymos, the Hungarian name of Iňačovce, on 22 August 1906 to Mihály Demkó and Mária Kocsis, both Greek Catholic. The father is a day-labourer born at Magasrév, aged 24. Magasrév is Viszoka, and a Mihály Demkó was baptised there on 20 August 1882, so the man in the first file given to this agent is very probably Maria's father, not her brother. Two links in that chain rest on names, places and ages agreeing and not on a record that says so; the marriage of Mihály Demkó and Mária Kocsis would close one of them. The registrar explained the entry to the father in Slovak. A petition of 1803 puts a Joannes Demko at Viszoka. A cropped baptism the collector marked 'maybe' has the wrong birthday and the wrong mother and is probably another child. Three hypotheses are confirmed, one refuted, six raised.

title: Ledger v3 and first cross-review: 22 strips taken from the Duska repo
blurb: Read ledger v3 and made the first cross-review pass over the Duska repo at ce326b4. Kevin had filed two folders of Demko baptisms under Duska; under the coordinator's ruling they are archived here too, with matching checksums, and read afresh before comparing. Twenty strips are from one book, and the book now identifies itself: its entries of the 1870s are signed by the Greek Catholic pastor of Csicser, and the entry of January 1883 writes 'Csurgovich János' in full. They rebuild the household that Maria Demko's father was born into. György Demkó and Mária Hreskó were married by January 1857, lost a daughter that year and twin boys in 1873, and had János in 1875, Borbála in 1879 and Mihály in 1882, moving from house 79 to 121 to 132. A János Demkó, probably a brother, farmed next door. A generation earlier, a György Demko appears at Viszoka with three different wives' names in nine years. Two boys of the 1830s are candidates for the György who married Mária Hreskó. This agent's readings agree with the Duska agent's on all but two points: the mother's rite in the 1857 entry, and a residence in 1873 that this agent could not read. The two Belža strips are also read; they concern another Demko family near Košice. Three Kocsis strips show no link to Maria's mother. Four hypotheses moved, three were raised.

title: Ledger v8: reused names, living status, provenance; second cross-review
blurb: Read ledger v8 and the coordinator's method note on epidemics and reused names, and applied them. The note bites on this line at once. The Mihály baptised at Viszoka in 1882 already carries the name of a twin brother who died in 1873, and nothing in hand shows that he himself lived: the burial books are not in the file. What speaks for him is the age his daughter's birth record gives her father in 1906, twenty-four, which fits the child of 1882 and not the dead twin. The link stays at 70 and is now marked as an unresolved necronym risk; so is the step from the Mária of 1906 to the Mary Demko who died in Montréal. The second cross-review of the Duska repo found a new folder, Iňačovce Greek Catholic, and six of its strips are taken here. They show Demkos already in that parish before the Viszoka Mihály arrived: a Michael Demko, cottar of Jesztreb, in 1870, and a 'Mihály Demkó the younger', cottar of Jesztreb, with a wife Anna in 1889. That second Mihály is very probably the father on the cropped 'maybe' baptism, which makes it another family's child. A Kocsis couple at Solymos in 1875 becomes the first candidate for the parents of Maria's mother. Living status now follows the coordinator's rule: Stefan Duska died in 2018, and his son's status is unknown. Every document carries a provenance block, mostly reading 'unknown'. The one photograph showing the subject of the tree is held, not published.

title: Demko Hints: three strips, and a third Mihály Demkó
blurb: A small folder the owner calls hints. One file is the cropped 'maybe' baptism again, this time named with a year: 1892. A second strip, in the same hand, shows the same parents five years earlier: Anna, born 19 September [1887] to Mihály Demkó, day-labourer, and Anna Batronszki (?), at a place read as Sztrajnyán, with a note that the entry was written in the wrong book. The third is Anna, illegitimate daughter of Ilona Demkó of Lasztomér, [1887]. Together they move the 'maybe' Mária further from Maria Demko of Iňačovce: she is fourteen years too old for the gravestone and her parents are a different couple in a different village. They also undo last batch's guess that her father was the Mihály Demkó of Jesztreb, whose wife had another surname. That makes three men called Mihály Demkó in one district in one generation, which is the plainest warning in the file against matching on a name. Read ledger v10: the only change is that the rule on reused names is craft knowledge and not a statement about this family. Third cross-review of the Duska repo found nothing new for this line. One hypothesis refuted, one strengthened, one raised.

title: Demko Military: four soldiers' cards; seven more Iňačovce strips
blurb: Four index cards for soldiers named Demko who died in the First World War; the folder's name says the Second, but the deaths are of 1915 to 1918. Andreas, born 1896 at Enyiczke, fell on Monte Asolone in Italy in April 1918. Gregor, a Galician from near Przemyśl, died in the epidemic hospital at Košice in March 1915. One Ján, born 1896 at Giňov, was killed in Bukovina on New Year's Day 1916. Another Ján, from Šariš, died a prisoner in a camp hospital at Samarkand in September 1915. None was born in Ung county and none can be tied to Maria Demko's people; the Giňov man may belong to the other Demko family already met in the Belža strips. The cross-review of the Duska repo was more useful to this line. Seven further strips from the Iňačovce Greek Catholic book are taken here. They name two Kocsis couples at Solymos, the village and surname of Maria's mother: János Kocsis and Anna Kováts at house 13 in 1875 and 1877, and Mihály Kocsis and Mária Knyezső at house 19 in 1889. Either could be the parents of the Mária Kocsis born there about 1886; no baptism of hers is in hand. The strips also show the name of a dead child reused twice among the Kocsis, and carry the Demkos of Jesztreb back to the 1820s. Three hypotheses raised, two revised, none resolved.

title: Ledgers v15 and v16; the first file from the Sorter's piles, a chart of another family with a second Mary D[e]mko born in 1906

What can be read is a woman called Mary, surname Demko or Danko, born in 1906 in America, apparently at Passaic in New Jersey, tied to Vysoká nad Uhom through her parents Andrej and Mária, and dead in the 1990s. Vysoká is the village Maria Demko's father came from, so this may be a branch of the same Demkos that went to America and came back. It is not Maria Demko herself: she was born at Solymos and died in Montréal in 1950. The two share a name and a birth year, which is how people get merged, so a guard is on the board. One correction to the last batch: this agent did open the owner's old memory note on his genealogy, in its first turn on 11 November, before the blind rule; the last batch said it had not.

title: Ledgers v17 and v18; a curiosities list; thirteen strips from the Reformed book of Solymos, all but two of them Knyezső

The cross-review brought thirteen strips from a folder the owner gave the Duska agent: baptisms from the Reformed register of Solymos, 1825 to 1921. Eleven are labelled Nyemcsik and every one reads Knyezső, the surname of the woman who may be Maria Demko's grandmother. The two strips labelled Kocsis have no Kocsis child; one has a Kocsis mother in 1825, the earliest of the name at Solymos. title: The Demko pile: Maria Demko's passport and the papers of her emigration in 1937, a second parish extract, and her husband's death notice
blurb: The Sorter has put eleven files in this agent's pile. Eight are photographs of one bundle: the papers on which Maria Demko left Czechoslovakia in 1937. Her emigrant's passport names her Maria Dušková, born Demková, and gives her birth as 22 August 1906 at Iňačovce. That is the day and place of the birth registration this line has rested on since the fourth batch, so the link between the baby of 1906 and the woman who married a Duska now stands on a paper she carried herself. The passport describes her: oblong face, grey eyes, chestnut hair. It has her photograph with her son, and her signature, Marja Duškova. The other papers give the journey. Her husband, Mike Duska of 1196a St. George Street, Montréal, applied to bring her and the boy over; Ottawa answered on 11 September; he paid $178.50 on the 17th; the court at Michalovce let the boy go on 7 October; and on 8 November in Prague she signed a contract to sail from Antwerp on the 11th by the Montrose. The landing itself is not in hand. In 1937 she was living at Iňačovce, her own village. A second extract of her son's baptism, made in 1955, agrees with the one of 1947 and settles the godmother: Zuzana Bandura. A death notice of 1974 gives her husband's death and a second son, Mike, entered by name only. The notice is held; so is the full photograph of the contract, which shows something from outside this experiment at its edge. The Duska agent's note had described these papers before this agent read its own copies, so the readings here are not blind. The ledger is unchanged at v19. Curiosities: 5.

title: Maria Demko in the census of 1930, with the date of her marriage; and a Demko at Viszoka in the urbarial table
blurb: Four pages from a folder the owner gave the Duska agent. The first is the household sheet of the 1930 census for Senné no. 145. Maria is there with her son, in her husband's father's house: Greek Catholic, Slovak by nationality, able to read and write, married on 30 January 1927 and living at Senné since that same day. Her husband is not in the house. That is the first date for her marriage; the entry itself is still missing, and it is the record that would name her parents. The sheet gives her birthday as 15 August 1907, where her passport says 22 August 1906. The census answer came from her in-laws and is the weaker of the two, but a second date a year later is what a reused name would look like, so the check stays open and that reading goes back up to 7. The other three pages are urbarial tables, small and undated on their face; the owner dates them 1767. At Viszoka, the village Maria's father came from, serf no. 6 of the convent of Lelesz is a Michael Demko with a whole holding. He is the earliest Demko in the file, a generation before the Joannes Demko of 1803. At Solymos a Gergely Kocsis holds a whole serf holding. Descent from either is not shown. Still to take: four Senné census sheets and 24 Senné baptism strips of Kocsis and Demko namesakes, and the Iňačovce and Vysoká census sheets when the Duska agent has them. Curiosities: 3.

title: Ledger v22; Maria Demko's father in the census of 1930, with a second wife, a son, and a mother-in-law named Kočišová
blurb: Ledger v22 is read. It asks this agent to say what kind of object each document is, from its form, before leaning on it; that is now a field on 25 documents. The green page of 1906 is a page of a Hungarian state birth register in the one-entry-to-a-page form used until 1906, signed by the registrar and by her father; which of the register's two copies it is cannot be told from the form. No document changes its name. Maria Demko's second son is entered as dead on the owner's word, and a file name that had hidden his name is restored. One census sheet is taken from the Duska agent: Iňačovce no. 117 on 1 December 1930, the house of Michal Demko, born at Vysoká on 28 August 1882. This is Maria's father. It shows the boy born at Viszoka in August 1882 grew up, which closes the survival check on him. His wife is Zuzanna, born 1901, married in 1919, so Maria's mother Mária Kocsis had died by then. A son Juraj, born 1911, is Maria's brother. And in the house is his mother-in-law, Maria Kočišová: a Roman Catholic widow, born at Iňačovce in 1863, married in 1879. That is what Mária Knyezső, the mother of the Mária Kocsis baptised in 1887, would look like forty years on. The sheet does not say which wife was her daughter, so the Kocsis question moves to the cap of 70 and not past it. Both capped links of the line are now firmer than the cap lets the board show; the record that would lift it is still the marriage of 1927, or one that names a parent. Curiosities: 3.
